title: Rutte Tells Ditchley Foundation NATO 3.0 Is a 'Rebalancing,' Warns of Most Dangerous Security Environment in a Generation
detail: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte delivered the Ditchley Foundation's 62nd Annual Lecture in Oxfordshire, UK, on September 16, 2026, telling the audience that 'NATO 3.0 is not a reboot, but a rebalancing of our security for the better' and that 'to stay transatlantic, NATO is becoming more European — a NATO with Europe, and Canada, spending more, producing more, and doing more for their security. This is the idea of NATO 3.0.' Rutte warned the alliance faces its 'most dangerous and complex' security environment in a generation, citing Russia's war against Ukraine and hybrid activity against allied territory, while framing the burden-shift to European conventional defense as a deliberate mutual project rather than a US retreat. The visit also included separate remarks with UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer. The lecture did not address the pending Pentagon force-posture review or troop-level options due to Defense Secretary Hegseth by November 6, leaving the core US-drawdown question — the alliance's most concrete Article 5-reliability test — unresolved even as Rutte's rhetorical framing of the transition stayed consistent with his September 10 Berlin remarks.
